text:
maya: heads-up — the embed rerank runner is flaking on the low-shot quant experiments. CI shows a reproducible ordering mismatch on mteb_sim_small when we run int8 artifacts vs fp16.

sam: saw that too. failing NDCG/MRR delta ~0.02 across a few queries. logs show different anchor selection order, not just score noise. :thinking_face:

alex: could be a sampling seed bug? the runner samples anchors for rerank ties using np.random.choice without a global seed. CI shards might be using different RNG states.

maya: exact mismatch excerpt from CI: \n```\nquery=Q123 score_list=[0.8934,0.8934,0.7120] original_order=[5,2,9] sampled_anchors=[2,5,9]\nnote: tie_between(0,1) resolved -> different tie-break than local run\n```\n
jordan: also noticed quantization rounding makes two previously-distinct scores collapse to identical floats in int8 path, increasing tie frequency. ties + non-deterministic sampling = flaky metrics.

sam: minimal repro: run eval_harness/runner.py::select_anchors with seed unset vs seed=42 on the small shard. when unset CI shows reorder. quick patch: pass explicit seed via env RUNNER_SEED to the runner init.

alex: here's a very small patch sketch we tried locally — deterministic RNG per-runner instance: \n```\n# runner.py\nseed = int(os.getenv('RUNNER_SEED', '0'))\nrng = np.random.default_rng(seed + shard_id)\nindices = rng.choice(candidates, size=k, replace=False)\n```\n
maya: that fix made local results match CI for me but we still see an NDCG drop when switching to int8 vs fp16 for low-shot anchors. seems like two issues: RNG determinism + quant rounding changing rank ties.

sam: propose CI change + harness test: 1) force RUNNER_SEED=2026 in eval CI matrix; 2) add a deterministic-anchor-sampling unit that asserts same order across quant configs when scores are sufficiently distinct (and explicitly warns when ties are expected).

jordan: agree. also we should change metric contract to document tie-handling: stable sort by (score, original_index) so ranking is deterministic even when scores tie due to quantization. small change and avoids sampling entirely for tie-breaks.

maya: good point — stable sort probably simpler than sampling. downside: for rerank we sometimes want random anchors for stress testing. maybe make sampling opt-in and stable sort the default deterministic fallback.

alex: I'll open a PR with two commits: (A) enforce stable tie-breaker in rerank sort, (B) CI change to set RUNNER_SEED and add the new unit test. linking draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/401 (WIP).

ci-bot: build 4023 failed on eval-harness/tests/test_anchor_determinism.py (flake). rerun_repro:start 1913056000

sam: I'll take ownership of the quant regression investigation. next steps: (1) run int8 vs fp16 pairwise diffs on mteb_sim_small and subset queries that show the biggest ordering changes, (2) log exact fp values pre-quant and post-quant to see rounding buckets, (3) check if increasing embedding dim or changing quant binning reduces tie frequency.

maya: thanks — if you want I can add a lightweight debug hook that dumps per-query score vectors and indices for failing CI shards only (gzipped). that will make triage faster.

sam: please do. add opt-in ENV DEBUG_RERANK_DUMP=true and include path in CI artifacts.

jordan: once the PR stabilizes we'll also add a dashboard test that tracks tie-rate and frequency of quant-induced reorders per model-variant. want to catch regressions early. :bar_chart:

maya: awesome. filing the follow-ups: \n- PR: enforce stable tie-break + seed opt-in (alex)\n- CI: set RUNNER_SEED in eval matrix + add test (alex/sam)\n- Debug dump hook (maya)\n- Quant diffs and stats (sam)\n- Dashboard alert for tie-rate drift (jordan)\n
sam: tagging @eng-oncall if CI keeps failing after PR. will ping here when I have the first diffs. :eyes:

maya: thanks all. I'll wait for alex's draft and then we'll iterate.
